THESE APPEALS HAVING BEEN HEARD AND RESERVED FOR JUDGMENT ON 03.07.2023 AND COMING ON FOR  MFA NO.476/2014 C/W  MFA NO.543/2014  3 PRONOUNCEMENT OF JUDGMENT THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:

2  JUDGMENT

In these two appeals, both the petitioner and the insurer have challenged the judgment and award dated 30.09.2013 passed in M.V.C. No.877/2011 by the Principal District Judge and Member M.A.C.T-1 at Hassan ('the Tribunal' in short).
2. M.F.A.No.476/2014 is filed by the petitioner whereas M.F.A.No.543/2014 is filed by the Insurance Company.
For the sake of convenience, the rank of the parties will be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. The brief facts of the case are that on 05.02.2011 at about 09:00 a.m., while the petitioner was walking on the left side of the road in front of one Siddappa's house on Heragu road at Kenchanahalli Village, a Tractor bearing No.KA-14/T- 6662 caused the accident due to which he suffered MFA NO.476/2014 C/W injuries on his right lower limb, right upper limb and face.
After first-aid at Heragu Government Hospital, he was admitted to S.C.Hospital, Hassan, then at Sanjeevini Hospital, Hassan.
He was under hospitalization for 20 days and underwent surgery for the fracture.
Seeking compensation, he has moved the Tribunal.

The claim was opposed by the Insurance Company on the ground that the Tractor in question was not involved in the accident,
fraud is played and said Tractor is fixed for the accident.
Though it has admitted the policy of insurance denied that the driver of the Tractor did not possess valid Driving Licence.

The Tribunal has framed an issue regarding the fraud apart from other issues and after taking the evidence of the parties, passed the impugned judgment awarding compensation of Rs.74,500/- and directing the respondents No.1 and 2/owner and insurer to satisfy the award with interest at 9% p.a.
Pleading inadequacy of compensation, the petitioner has filed his appeal and MFA NO.476/2014 C/W challenging the very accident, the Insurance Company has filed its appeal.

4. Heard the arguments of Sri.Chethan. B, learned Counsel for the petitioner and Smt.H.R.Renuka, learned Counsel for the Insurance Company.
5.
It is the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner that the accident is genuine, the delay in filing the complaint is taken advantage by the Insurance Company to deny the accident.

On 05.02.2011, the injured was taken to hospital, he was under hospitalization for 20 days and he was under the impression that the complaint was filed by one Lokesh, who carried him to the hospital, but on 17.02.2011, he filed the complaint.

When the petitioner underwent surgery and he was bed-ridden, the delay in filing the complaint cannot be considered as fraud,
immediately after arriving at the hospital, the history of the accident is furnished MFA NO.476/2014 C/W and therefore, the Insurance Company cannot dispute the accident.

He has further submitted that the compensation awarded under the different heads is disproportionate to the nature of injury sustained, money spent towards treatment, also the disability suffered and sought for enhancement of Narasimha Shetty vs Manjegowda on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145374109/
3 compensation.
6.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance company has contended that the domestic enquiry conducted by the Insurance Company reveals that the owner of the Tractor was driving the Tractor at the time of accident and not the person charge sheeted by the police.

In this regard, the Insurance Company has recorded the statement of respondent No.1/owner of the Tractor and therefore, fraud is played by the petitioner for the sake of compensation and therefore, the claim petition deserves to be dismissed.
Apart from this, learned counsel also supported the impugned judgment MFA NO.476/2014 C/W insofar as for assessment of compensation is concerned.
7. I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments advanced on both sides and also perused the materials on record.

8. Having regard to the above, the two points that arise for consideration in these two appeals are:
(i) Whether the accident is genuine?
(ii) Whether the compensation assessed by the Tribunal is just compensation or not?
9.
With regard to the first point is concerned, before the Tribunal, the petitioner has examined himself as PW-1 and relied upon as many as seven documents as per Exs.P1 to P7.
It is pertinent to note that Ex.P1(a) is the statement of the petitioner recorded at Sanjeevini Hospital on 13.02.2011.
The complaint is also annexed with belated Police intimation dated 09.02.2011 which was received by MFA NO.476/2014 C/W the Police on 13.02.2011.
During this period, the hospital records clearly point out that the petitioner was impatient and he underwent surgery.
The hospital records clearly point out that the petitioner was brought to Sanjeevini Hospital at 05:30 p.m. on 06.02.2011 with a history of accident at Heragu.

It is contended by Smt.H.R.Renuka, learned counsel for the Insurance Company that the internal investigation conducted on behalf of the Insurance Company brought out that the insured Manjegowda himself was on the wheels at the time of accident and he did not possess any Driving Licence.

The driver proposed in the charge sheet is the owner of two tractors and he never go as hired driver, and it is a case where fraud played for the sake of compensation.
10.
The objections taken by the Insurance Company before the Tribunal points out that the tractor was not involved in the accident and its MFA NO.476/2014 C/W driver did not hold valid Driving Licence.

Except this, there is no reference as to the internal investigation conducted by the Insurance Company to explain that the respondent No.1 was on the wheels at the time of accident,
only in the appeal for the first time, this has been brought out.
When such a plea was not taken before the Tribunal, the Insurance Company cannot be permitted to raise such a ground in the appeal to attack the impugned judgment.
I have carefully perused the impugned judgment.

The Tribunal has evaluated the contention taken by the Insurance Company regarding non-involvement of the tractor and recorded its finding that at the time of accident, one H.N.Shivashankar was on the wheels of the tractor and it is he, who has caused the accident.
For this reason, he has been charge sheeted for the offences punishable under Sections 279 and 338 of I.P.C. as evidenced by Ex.P3/charge sheet.
The Insurance Company has not questioned the prosecution of the said driver.

sentences.text: Whatever the MFA NO.476/2014 C/W internal investigation conducted by the Insurance Company is for its internal purpose and it has no legal sanctity.

Hence, though the accident took place on 05.02.2011, the petitioner was under hospitalization, late intimation was sent to the Police by the hospital authorities only on 09.02.2011 and the statement of the injured was recorded on 13.02.2011 to set the law into motion.
Hence, I do not find any force in the arguments addressed on behalf of the Insurance Company.
I do not find any error or illegality committed by the Tribunal in accepting the alleged accident.

11. Adverting to the second point, the assessment of compensation by the Tribunal,
the impugned judgment points out different heads in arriving at Rs.74,500/- as the compensation, which is tabled as below:
Rs.
1. Towards pain and suffering 25,000-00 2.
Towards medical expenses 6,500-00 MFA NO.476/2014 C/W 3.
Towards attendant charges 1,000-00 4.
Towards conveyance charges 1,000-00 5.
Towards food and nourishment 1,000-00 charges 6.
Towards fracture of bones 30,000-00 7.
Towards loss of comfort 5,000-00 8.
Towards loss of expectation of 5,000-00 life

At page No.8 of the judgment, so also the medical records, the Tribunal referred the injuries sustained by the petitioner as follows:
"1) Fracture of medial malleolus right.
2) Fracture of calcanium right.
3) Fracture last tip malleolus under placed.
4) Irregular lacerated 3 x 5 cm last aspect of right ankle.
5) Abrasion 3 x 4 cm right maxillary area.

5 6) contusion 7 x 7 right shoulder.
7) Abrasion left foot."
13.

sentences.text: The medical records also pointed out that the petitioner was under hospitalization for 20 days and he has also spent money.
The records also point out that the petitioner is an agriculturist and MFA NO.476/2014 C/W aged 42 years.
Medical bills of Sanjeevini Hospital point out that a sum of Rs.6,372/- was spent for treatment, which the Tribunal assessed Rs.6,500/- towards medical expenses.

Having regard to three fractures sustained by the petitioner and also injury to his right ankle, right shoulder, right maxillary area and left foot, a sum of Rs.25,000/- assessed towards pain and suffering is on lower side, it ought to be Rs.30,000/-.

Towards attendant charges, a sum of Rs.2,000/-, towards travelling expenses, a sum of Rs.1,000/-, towards food and nourishment a sum of Rs.4,000/- and towards loss of amenities and discomfort at Rs.30,000/- is just and proper.
The petitioner being laid-up for a minimum of 20 days of hospitalization.
Hence, he has to be compensated towards loss of income during laid up period of 4 months.
The accident is of the year 2011 and the notional income that would be assessed could be not less than Rs.6,500/- and therefore, a sum of Rs.26,000/- has to be awarded.
The petitioner has MFA NO.476/2014 C/W not examined the Medical Officer, who treated him and therefore, it is not proper to assess on the disability.

Thus, the petitioner is entitled to total compensation of Rs.99,500/-, which is tabled herebelow:
Sl.No. Particulars Amount  (Rs.)
1. Pain and suffering 30,000-00 2.
Medical expenses 6,500-00 3. Attendant charges 2,000-00 4.
Travelling expenses 1,000-00 5. Food and nourishment 4,000-00 6. Loss of amenities and discomfort 30,000-00 7. Loss of income during laid up 26,000-00  period
Total 99,500

Total compensation comes to Rs.99,500/- instead of Rs.74,500/- assessed by the Tribunal,
thereby enhancement of Rs.25,000/-, it is just compensation in the facts and circumstances of the case.

15. As discussed above, the contention of the Insurance Company that fraud played by the MFA NO.476/2014 C/W petitioner for the sake of compensation cannot be sustained and the compensation assessed by the Tribunal is on the lower side
and therefore, the appeal filed by the petitioner deserves to be allowed and the appeal filed by the Insurance Company is devoid of merits.

In the result, the following:
ORDER Narasimha Shetty vs Manjegowda on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145374109/

(i) M.F.A.No.476/2014 filed by the petitioner is allowed in part.
(ii) M.F.A.No.543/2014 filed by the Insurance Company is dismissed.
(ii) The impugned judgment is modified accordingly.

(iii) The appellant/petitioner would be entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.25,000/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum on the enhanced compensation from the date of petition till its realization.
MFA NO.476/2014 C/W (iv) The respondent/Insurance Company is directed to deposit the enhanced compensation within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
(v) The amount in deposit, if any, shall be transmitted to the Tribunal along with records forthwith.
